input.description: An audit sample shows five reimbursement claims with altered totals and bank transfers to an account not listed for the relevant suppliers.
A treasurer reports that the same supplier invoice appears to have been paid twice, but the bank reference, approval record, and any refund information are not available.
A synthetic cash log is short by a substantial amount across four events, and the assigned custodian cannot produce deposit slips for any of the affected dates.
One ledger export marks an expense as approved while a meeting note says approval was deferred. It is unclear whether money was transferred, whether either record is final, or who entered the data.

A synthetic annual review lists a repeated pattern across twelve monthly expense batches. January contained two unsupported travel claims; February contained a supplier payment without an invoice; March contained a reimbursement approved by the recipient; April contained three altered receipt totals; May contained a payment to an account not present in the supplier register; June contained a duplicate equipment invoice; July contained cash withdrawals without event records; August contained a transfer described differently in the ledger and bank statement; September contained missing approval minutes; October contained an unexplained reversal; November contained another duplicate invoice; and December contained a large year-end transfer without supporting documents. The report includes the dates and amounts but does not include the original receipts, approval identities, supplier confirmations, or explanations for the discrepancies.
